## TRA Timeline

#### IPO and TRA execution

- 2021-10-04: Form-of TRA filed as Exhibit 10.15 to the S-1
- 2021-10-28: Executed TRA dated as of preamble, 85% of realized tax benefits on Pre-IPO Tax Benefits to General Atlantic, Trident/Stone Point, and Conrad
- 2021-11-02: IPO closes
- 2021-11-05: 8-K reports IPO close and attaches the executed TRA

#### Take-private with narrowly scoped CoC waiver

- 2024-02-15: General Atlantic Support Agreement waives Section 4.1(c) Change of Control acceleration solely for the Hearts Parent merger; all other TRA rights and obligations remain in full force
- 2024-06-28: Hearts Parent merger closes; HireRight delists and announces Form 25/15 deregistration; TRA persists at the surviving corporation but ceases SEC reporting

## Explanation

HireRight executed its Tax Receivable Agreement at the October 2021 IPO of the Delaware C-corp (no Up-C structure), committing to pay General Atlantic, Trident/Stone Point, and Raymond Conrad 85% of the realized federal, state, and local tax savings from the firm's Pre-IPO Tax Benefits (principally pre-IPO net operating losses and other carryforward attributes). The Q1 2024 10-Q recorded a $162.7M long-term portion after a $27.2M Q1 2024 payment, indicating the contract was generating substantive cash flows. In February 2024, as a condition to the Hearts Parent take-private, General Atlantic as TRA Party Representative narrowly waived only the Section 4.1(c) Change of Control acceleration tied to the Hearts merger; the contract otherwise remained in full force and was not terminated, amended elsewhere, or bought out. The merger closed June 28, 2024 and HireRight ceased SEC reporting; the TRA persists at the surviving private subsidiary but its post-close payment trajectory is not visible on EDGAR. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
